description: Macro-model convergence (kappa), shear (gamma), magnification (mu, signed by parity) at the positions of the five SN Refsdal images, from the v3 GLAFIC cluster mass model (Kawamata et al. 2016; Oguri 2010), as tabulated by Kelly et al. 2023 (ApJ 948, 93; arXiv:2305.06377) for the microlensing/millilensing magnification analysis.

provenance.primary_reference: Kelly et al. 2023, ApJ 948, 93 (arXiv:2305.06377), lensing-parameters table (GLAFIC v3)
provenance.transcription_note: Values transcribed via automated web extraction (ar5iv HTML of arXiv:2305.06377), corroborated by (i) two independent extractions returning identical kappa, (ii) internal consistency of (kappa,gamma,mu,parity) under mu = 1/[(1-kappa)^2 - gamma^2], and (iii) the SX/S1 magnification ratio 4.2/14.6 = 0.29 matching the Kelly+2023 measured value 0.30.
provenance.verification_status: confirmed against archived GLAFIC v3 maps (2026-09-25): at the published image positions below, the archived kappa map sampled bilinearly and rescaled by beta(z_s) = D_ls/D_s = 0.5339 reproduces all five tabulated kappa values to ~1-3% (uniform map/table ratio 1.878 vs 1/beta = 1.873 expected), and gamma values to ~3-8%.
provenance.map_normalization: The archived GLAFIC v3 maps (psi, kappa, gamma1, gamma2) are scaled to D_LS/D_OS = 1 (equivalently z_s -> infinity), per the GLAFIC v3 HLSP readme (Kawamata, Oguri & Ishigaki 2015). To convert any sampled kappa/gamma/psi to the SN Refsdal source plane z_s = 1.489, multiply by beta = D_ls/D_s = 0.5339 (z_l = 0.542, FlatLambdaCDM H0=70 Om0=0.3). An earlier ~4x map-vs-table mismatch traced to erroneous image positions (~10 arcsec north of the true field); it was not a map defect.
provenance.position_provenance: S1-S4: observed HST positions (ATel #6729; Karman et al. 2016, A&A, MUSE Table 1). SX: refined strong-lensing model position (Karman+2016 Table 1, Grillo et al.), coincident with the Kelly+2016 detection of 2015-12-11. Earlier pipeline versions used incorrect positions ~10 arcsec north (Dec ~22.398), sampling the cluster core rather than the image field.

key_physical_note: kappa_SX = 0.966 is the HIGHEST of the five images (SX lies in a high-convergence, near-critical region, at the smallest cluster-centric radius ~9.3 arcsec vs 12-14 arcsec for S1-S4). Under beta_A = -1 the TEP scalar field tracks the local Newtonian potential/density (same Poisson source), so the projected-density ordering identifies SX as the deepest temporal environment: slowest transport, latest arrival -- matching the observed +30.1 d residual sign. The flux ratio placing SX lowest is the same statement in the shallowness convention (low mu norm -> high Gamma under kappa_lens < 0); the apparent sign inversion when kappa is fed directly into the flux-calibrated formula is a depth-vs-shallowness convention artefact, not a physical contradiction.
